result.title: TempShap: When and How Much a Feature Matters in Time-Series Forecasting
result.summary: Attribution for a time-series forecaster should answer two questions that a feature-level scalar cannot: when in the input window a feature acts, and how much its influence changes across the forecast horizon. Most existing Shapley explainers treat each feature as one player and therefore collapse both axes. We propose TempShap, a retrospective, loss-based Shapley framework whose players are the individual input cells $(t,i)$. Its attribution tensor yields temporal-localization and horizon-impact profiles. We validate these against planted temporal structures, a tractable exact cell game, and a closed-form attribution oracle for a real linear forecaster. Permutation sharing estimates the cell-level game at localized perturbation cost. Under redundant inputs, one-at-a-time scores under-credit substitutable information, whereas the signed Shapley decomposition preserves total value and yields more reliable held-out deletion rankings under mean masking. A planted counterexample isolates the redundancy mechanism. Experiments show a deletion-ranking advantage across Shapley estimators, forecasting benchmarks, and model families. TempShap therefore makes fine-grained Shapley attribution both practical and operationally useful.

AI.brief_summary: TempShap 提出一种事后、基于损失的 Shapley 归因框架，把 player 细化到输入矩阵的单个单元格 (t,i)，输出时间定位与预测期影响轮廓，并用置换共享在局部扰动代价下估计该单元格博弈。
AI.relevance_reason: 其细粒度时序归因及冗余输入下带符号 Shapley 分解保留总价值的做法，可能为判断 latent 推理轨迹中各步或各视觉证据的实际贡献提供借鉴，但跨域迁移到 VLM 推理的可行性需核查。
